input.name: opencode-migration-check
input.prompt:
The user (in the coding-agent-landscape research conversation) just asked: "Should we consider moving to OpenCode? What are the drawbacks of doing so? Could we leverage similar plugin models that would allow us to deploy the equivalent of agent teams and workflows? What enhancements does OpenCode provide over Claude [Code]? Can it be driven remotely?"

Context you already have from this conversation's prior research (do not re-derive, just build on it): opencode (sst/opencode, MIT) now has ~161-180k GitHub stars (out-starring Claude Code's ~135k), 75+ providers via Models.dev plus dedicated Moonshot AI (Kimi K2) and Z.AI (GLM-4.7) provider integrations and Qwen3 Coder via its own "OpenCode Zen" tier. It has a mature per-custom-agent `model:` override (agent config overrides global) — the strongest documented option for genuinely heterogeneous Kimi/GLM/Qwen/Claude/GPT teams. Its agent system distinguishes primary agents (Build, Plan) from subagents (General, Explore, Scout), configurable via opencode.json or markdown+YAML frontmatter with fine-grained per-tool permission maps (allow/ask/deny, glob-scoped bash rules). Its plugin architecture is a JS/TS event-driven hook system (tool.execute.before/after, session.created/compacted/updated, message.*, lsp.*, tui.prompt.append/tui.command.execute/tui.toast.show, permission.asked/permission.replied) — materially lower-level/more programmable than Claude Code's manifest+skill model. Its TUI is built on OpenTUI (a from-scratch Zig-core terminal engine). It has REAL reliability complaints as of a recent HN thread ("Annoying and alarming things about OpenCode"): heavy memory/CPU use, a fast-breaking release cadence, buggy autocompact/compaction, and a since-fixed December 2025 RCE. As of the most recent check, native isolated-workspace multi-agent orchestration (an actual Claude-Code-Agent-Teams equivalent) was an OPEN GitHub feature request (anomalyco/opencode#17994, "Support for multi-agent orchestration in isolated workspaces") — not yet shipped natively — filled in the meantime by a community port (a dev.to writeup by uenyioha porting Claude Code's Agent Teams concept onto opencode, notably adding the ability to mix models from different providers in one team, which stock Claude Code cannot do). There's also an unresolved GitHub issue (~Jan 2026, #6930) about whether routing a Claude Pro/Max subscription through opencode is a gray-area ToS violation. Existing Claude Code SKILL.md-based skills are NOT directly compatible with opencode's agent format and would need porting/rewriting.

Your job: do fresh, source-cited web research (WebSearch/WebFetch) to answer specifically:

1. STATUS CHECK: Has anomalyco/opencode#17994 (or any equivalent native multi-agent/team orchestration feature) shipped in opencode as of now? Check the opencode GitHub repo's recent releases/changelog and docs directly. If it's still open/unshipped, say so with the issue's current state. If a native "team" feature exists now, describe exactly what it does and how mature it is.

2. REMOTE DRIVING: Can opencode be "driven remotely" in any of these senses — (a) a headless/server/API mode that lets another process or a web UI drive a session without a local interactive TUI, (b) a hosted/cloud session equivalent to Claude Code's claude.ai/code web sessions or --cloud/--teleport, (c) a mobile app or web dashboard for monitoring/interacting with a running session from a phone, (d) first-class CI/GitHub Actions integration for triggering runs. Check opencode's own docs (opencode.ai/docs) directly for a "server", "headless", "API", "remote", or "web" mode/command, and check for any official or widely-used third-party solution (e.g. does something like Claude Squad/ccmanager style remote access exist, or an opencode-specific equivalent). Be precise about what's officially documented vs. community/DIY (e.g. "just SSH into a machine running the TUI" doesn't count as a real remote-driving feature — look for something more specific: an actual server/API/web/mobile surface).

3. ENHANCEMENTS OVER CLAUDE CODE: Beyond what's already known (multi-vendor model support, permission granularity, OpenTUI), find 2-3 more concrete things opencode does better or differently than Claude Code as of 2026 — e.g. cost/pricing model differences, specific UX features, editor/IDE integration breadth, config portability, session/context handling, or anything else substantive found in recent (2026) comparison articles, official docs, or credible user reports. Cite sources.

4. MIGRATION DRAWBACKS, CONCRETE: Beyond what's already known (SKILL.md porting needed, no native team-equivalent yet, general reliability complaints, ToS gray area on Claude subscription reuse), find any additional concrete drawbacks specifically relevant to migrating a Claude-Code-plugin-based repository (this user's repo: orin-dx/agent-plugins, built around plugin.json manifests, SKILL.md skills, subagent .md files, hooks.json, and a plugin marketplace) — e.g., does opencode have an equivalent plugin marketplace/distribution mechanism at all, or is plugin distribution purely DIY/npm-based? How mature is opencode's hooks lifecycle compared to Claude Code's 14-17+ hook events? Is there any migration tooling or guide for porting Claude Code plugins/skills to opencode specifically?

Only assert what you can source (URL + date), mark confidence honestly, and say clearly when something is unconfirmed or you couldn't find it. Do not pad with generic priors.

Report back a structured summary organized under these same 4 headings, each with concrete findings and sources. Keep it tight — this feeds a direct chat answer, not another report section. Under 600 words in your final summary, but include the source URLs.
